description:
The release archive carries the default vocabulary package as well, so a repository can obtain everything it needs from one download once the binary writes no configuration of its own.

## Background

The workflow package already rides in the archive. Two things then make a second directory necessary rather than tidy. The workflow package declares a dependency on the default package and no longer restates its vocabulary, so applying it from the archive resolves nothing unless the dependency is there beside it. And a bare initialization is about to stop writing any vocabulary at all, so a repository that applies no package has none — which is the intent, but only if a package is obtainable.

The mechanism exists: the staging step and the member list the workflow package's directory established take a second directory unchanged. What is new is the dependency the smoke path can now observe. Asserting that the default package was applied as a resolved dependency is the release's best end-to-end evidence that composition works from published bytes, so the step is strengthened rather than merely extended.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The archive carries the default package directory beside the workflow package, under the same directory the workflow package uses.
- [hard] REQ-02: The published asset set is still unchanged, and the existing checksum file still covers both.
- [hard] REQ-03: The archive-verification step asserts both package directories are present.
- [hard] REQ-04: The smoke path applies the workflow package from the extracted archive and asserts that the default package was applied as its resolved dependency.

## Notes

This is a hard predecessor of removing the configuration the binary writes: without it, that removal leaves a release in which a fresh repository can obtain no vocabulary at all.
title: Carry the default package in the release archive too
